title: UNCERTAIN: f89r2 fragment 35 has a label and shares a lobed crown with f35v
sources: René Zandbergen, Villa Mondragone presentation (2012), PDF p. 24 https://voynich.nu/papers/Voynich100_RZ_2012.pdf and https://www.voynich.nu/q15/index.html
Siv Bugge Vatne, The Morphology of the Voynich Plants (2022), p. 8 https://crackingthevoynichcipher.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/5_the_morphology_of_the_voynich_plants_siv_bugge_vatne_2022.pdf
Pinned transliterations ZL3b, RF1b, IT2a and GC2a, locus f89r2.4
statement: I checked both Yale scans. Fragment 35, third plant in the top row of f89r2, has a broad rounded-lobed green crown with several stalks converging on a thick brown spreading base. The label is under the crown and to the right of its stalks. ZL3b and RF1b join it as saloiinsheol, IT2a separates saloiin.sheol, and GC2a gives saeom3coe. Zandbergen compares fragment 35 with f35v, which has a similar crown and a broad brown root. The fragment lacks the twining branches and separate berry-like clusters that make the f35v comparison with edera nigra in BnF Latin 6823 f60r plausible. I inspected that BnF illustration via the reproduction in Zandbergen's slides because the Gallica scan returned 403. Vatne endorses the f35v comparison and notes that the Voynich drawing lacks the comparator's ivy leaves. The two discussions use the same BnF image. The fragment's crown alone cannot distinguish oak, ivy, a composite, or a conventional leaf form. The manuscript label is a candidate for an internal image match, with its language and meaning still open.
